To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the area that extends past the corner is essential to recover the hidden scene, 2) the area that is visible from the accessible scene is sufficient for object identification, and 3 ) a combination of data-driven models with geometric understanding is necessary to recover the hidden object

1) we introduce a method to localize and identify objects hidden around corners with consumer camera, 2) we show that the area that extends behind the corner is essential in the accessible scene for object identification and localization, and 3), we show the first step of how flash photography can be used to recover the hidden scene in 3D

1) the area that extends past the corner contains information about the hidden object, 2) this information can be extracted using a data-driven model, and 3), this model can be used for both object localization and identification
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of recovering the hidden scene from the accessible scene using only flash photography.
how to use the accessible scene to infer the hidden object.

the following questions: 1) Can we use consumer flash photography to recover the hidden scene in a data-driven way? 2) Can we localize and identify a hidden object with a single image? and 3) Can we reconstruct the hidden scene in 3D from a single image?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method is the first that combines geometric understanding and data driven methods to recover the hidden scene from the accessible scene.
the proposed method can localize and identify a wide class of objects around corners with high accuracy.
our proposed approach is a first step towards flash based data-driven NLOS scene reconstruction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the first steps towards data-driven hidden scene recovery using flash photography.
we can localize and identify hidden objects with a consumer camera, even if we can’t see them.
flash photography can be used to localize, identify, and even reconstruct the hidden scene around corners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information about the hidden object can be encoded in the accessible scene in a way that is not obvious to human observers.
, with careful data collection, we can train deep networks to recover hidden objects from a single flash image.
a data-driven method can be trained on rendered samples to recover a hidden scene from real data, without any additional training data.
